subject: zoology
question_text: Define incubation period. What is its duration in the life cycle of Plasmodium vivax?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: The period between the entry of the sporozoites
into the blood of man and the appearance of the
first symptoms of malaria is called the
steps.why: This period is measured from entry to SYMPTOMS, so it ends only when enough red blood cells burst together to give the first chill and fever.
common_mistakes: Defining it as the gap between two entries into the blood. That is the prepatent period.
Starting the count from the mosquito bite in general. Start it from the entry of the sporozoites.
steps.memory_tip: Incubation ends with the first fever; prepatent ends with the parasite back in the blood.
steps.margin_note: One sentence, ending at the word symptoms. That word carries the mark.

steps.label: Duration
lines: The first chill and fever of malaria appear at
steps.why: The number is asked directly, and it is always longer than the prepatent period because symptoms need several erythrocytic cycles to build up.
common_mistakes: Writing 8 days. That is the prepatent period.
Writing 48 hours. That is the length of one erythrocytic cycle.
steps.memory_tip: Three numbers, three meanings: 48 hours one cycle, 8 days prepatent, 10 to 14 days incubation.
steps.margin_note: The number in a box and one line on the first fever. Two lines.

insider_note: Examiners set prepatent and incubation next to each other, so name the endpoint (symptoms) as well as the number.
